raw_graphql_pull_request.body: Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/18262 and removes a longstanding hotfix that I think was used to bypass this issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/947a14d617f02b95fc1a04061810a73a2db962d1/python/sglang/srt/server_args.py#L4881-L4884 A fix for the same issue was attempted at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20890 but is IMO not correct. ## Motivation By default, AITER attention backend needs memory depending on `max_total_num_tokens`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/495ae9aaa609d39fd4e294d4f64faf52e29f50a6/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py#L270-L277 and `max_total_num_tokens` itself does not take it into account, ending up defining too large `max_total_num_tokens` and too large KV cache, leaving not enough space for AITER attention backend buffer, resulting in OOM errors or in exceeding the `mem_fraction_static` static. Example crash: `sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 1` on MI355: ``` [2026-07-15 09:39:22] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 2227073, K size: 101.95 GB, V size: 101.95 GB [2026-07-15 09:39:22] Memory pool end. avail mem=60.65 GB [2026-07-15 09:39:24] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4361, in run_scheduler_process scheduler = Scheduler( File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 424, in __init__ self.init_model_worker() File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 853, in init_model_worker self.init_all_attention_backends() File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 351, in init_attention_backends self.model_runner.init_attention_backends() File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 908, in init_attention_backends self.init_attention_backend() File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 2459, in init_attention_backend self.attn_backend = self._get_attention_backend() File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 2515, in _get_attention_backend attn_backend = self._get_attention_backend_from_str( File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py", line 92, in create_aiter_backend return AiterAttnBackend(runner) File "/felmarty/repos/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py", line 271, in __init__ self.workspace_buffer = torch.empty( torch.OutOfMemoryError: HIP out of memory. Tried to allocate 65.00 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 287.98 GiB of which 60.43 GiB is free. Of the allocated memory 224.04 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 2.26 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation. See documentation for Memory Management (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda.html#environment-variables) [2026-07-15 09:39:24] Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed. [2026-07-15 09:39:24] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=17757, include_parent=True, pid=17757 ``` See context and details in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/18262 ## Solution See the comment: ``` Solve for the KV byte budget that jointly accounts for the KV cache and the aiter attention workspace. We need to satisfy: - kv_budget + aiter_workspace_bytes = available_bytes - aiter_workspace_bytes = max_num_reqs * W - max_num_reqs = clamp(max_total_num_tokens * 512 / context_len, 2048, 4096), i.e. max_num_reqs ~= clamp(kv_budget * 512 / (context_len * cell_size), 2048, 4096) as max_total_num_tokens = kv_budget // cell_size. The `max_num_reqs` function is piecewise. We solve for each piece and pick the valid solution: - Case 1: kv_budget * 512 / (context_len * cell_size) <= 2048 - Case 2: 2048 <= kv_budget * 512 / (context_len * cell_size) <= 4096 - Case 3: kv_budget * 512 / (context_len * cell_size) >= 4096 ``` ## Example ### `sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tensor-parallel-size 1` - On `main` + 1xMI355: **crashes at AITER attention buffer allocation** (not enough space left despite the workaround `mem_fraction_static *= 0.85` on main - On this branch + 1xMI355: `KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 1896562, K size: 86.82 GB, V size: 86.82 GB` ### `sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tensor-parallel-size 1` - On `main` + 1xMI355: ``` [2026-07-15 13:17:24] Load weight end. elapsed=16.58 s, type=Qwen3MoeForCausalLM, avail mem=230.20 GB, mem usage=56.98 GB. self.server_args.mem_fraction_static 0.77435 [2026-07-15 13:17:25] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 1806426, K size: 82.69 GB, V size: 82.69 GB [2026-07-15 13:17:25] Memory pool end. avail mem=61.18 GB ###### self.workspace_buffer size: 55.99 GB ... Capturing batches (bs=512 avail_mem=3.89 GB): 0%| | 0/52 [00:00 **Allocating lower `max_total_num_tokens` is intended**. Current `main` branch is wrongfully over-allocating KV cache buffer (and AITER attention buffer), resulting in exceeding the budget of `total_memory * mem_fraction_static`. We see that only ~5 GB is left available after that, even risking OOM in CUDA Graph capture or elsewhere. ### Unified attention case: `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_VERIFY=1 sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tensor-parallel-size 1` - On `main` + 1xMI355: ``` [2026-07-15 13:59:38] Load weight end. elapsed=16.38 s, type=Qwen3MoeForCausalLM, avail mem=230.20 GB, mem usage=56.98 GB. [2026-07-15 13:59:39] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 1806426, K size: 82.69 GB, V size: 82.69 GB [2026-07-15 13:59:39] Memory pool end. avail mem=61.18 GB ``` - On this branch + 1xMI355: ``` [2026-07-15 13:57:45] Load weight end. elapsed=16.25 s, type=Qwen3MoeForCausalLM, avail mem=230.20 GB, mem usage=56.98 GB. self.server_args.mem_fraction_static 0.911 [2026-07-15 13:57:46] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 2235118, K size: 102.32 GB, V size: 102.32 GB [2026-07-15 13:57:46] Memory pool end. avail mem=21.42 GB ``` The over-reservation of `mem_fraction_static *= 0.85` is clear here. ## MLA case Aiter attention backends also allocates buffers for MLA case, see: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/495ae9aaa609d39fd4e294d4f64faf52e29f50a6/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py#L380-L401 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/495ae9aaa609d39fd4e294d4f64faf52e29f50a6/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py#L474-L489 These buffer sizes come from https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/7c6a0ba5c9cf7b45b2fce42f3aa66a30ef627d7b/aiter/ops/attention.py#L1135 and are typically negligible <10 MB, meaning that the ~43 GB that the 0.85 factor was reserving on a 287 GB GPU was a clear over-reservation. So removing the `mem_fraction_static *= 0.85` workaround is safe IMO. ## CUDA graph buffers The CUDA-graph related buffers as https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/495ae9aaa609d39fd4e294d4f64faf52e29f50a6/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py#L1423-L1427 are already taken care of in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/495ae9aaa609d39fd4e294d4f64faf52e29f50a6/python/sglang/srt/server_args.py#L4024 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #29416857841](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29416857841) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #29416857566](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29416857566)

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a dynamic calculation for `max_num_total_tokens` to prevent Out-Of-Memory errors when using the AITER attention backend. The core of the change is a new method, `_solve_max_tokens_with_aiter_workspace`, which correctly accounts for the AITER workspace memory by solving a piecewise function. This is a significant improvement over the previous static memory allocation. The removal of the related heuristic in `server_args.py` is also a good cleanup. I've included one suggestion to address a potential oversight where the workspace memory is not accounted for when `max_running_requests` is explicitly set, which could still lead to OOMs.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The current logic correctly handles the dynamic calculation of `max_total_num_tokens` when `max_running_requests` is not set. However, when `max_running_requests` is specified, the code falls through to the `else` block, which does not account for the AITER workspace memory. This could still lead to Out-Of-Memory errors, which this pull request aims to fix.

To make this more robust, I suggest handling the fixed `max_running_requests` case explicitly for the `aiter` backend by calculating the workspace size and subtracting it from the available memory. This ensures memory is correctly provisioned in all scenarios for the `aiter` backend.

```python
        if (
            self.server_args.attention_backend == "aiter"
            and self.mambaish_config is None
        ):
            from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import AttentionArch
            if self.model_config.attention_arch == AttentionArch.MLA:
                # For MLA, workspace is allocated dynamically, not during init
                max_total_num_tokens = rest_memory_bytes // cell_size
            elif self.server_args.max_running_requests is None:
                # `max_total_num_tokens` is used in `ModelRunnerKVCacheMixin.init_memory_pool` to define
                # `max_num_reqs`, which is in turn used in AITER attention backend to define GPU HBM buffers for the attention.
                # The default strategy below to resolve `max_total_num_tokens` does NOT take into account the memory required for the attention backend, potentially resulting in OOM errors in AITER buffers allocation.
                max_total_num_tokens = self._solve_max_tokens_with_aiter_workspace(
                    rest_memory_bytes, cell_size, num_layers
                )
            else:
                # When max_running_requests is set, max_num_reqs is fixed.
                # We need to account for the AITER workspace memory.
                from sglang.srt.layers.attention.aiter_backend import AiterAttnBackend
                num_head = self.model_config.num_attention_heads // get_attention_tp_size()
                head_dim = self.model_config.head_dim
                max_context_len = self.model_config.context_len
                max_num_partitions = AiterAttnBackend.get_max_num_partitions(max_context_len)
                W = num_head * max_num_partitions * (head_dim * 4 + 8)
                max_num_reqs = self.server_args.max_running_requests
                aiter_workspace = max_num_reqs * W
                max_total_num_tokens = (rest_memory_bytes - aiter_workspace) // cell_size
        else:
            # No workspace overhead for other backends
            max_total_num_tokens = rest_memory_bytes // cell_size
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The current logic correctly handles the dynamic calculation of `max_total_num_tokens` when `max_running_requests` is not set. However, when `max_running_requests` is specified, the code falls through to the `else` block, which does not account for the AITER workspace memory. This could still lead to Out-Of-Memory errors, which this pull request aims to fix.

To make this more robust, I suggest handling the fixed `max_running_requests` case explicitly for the `aiter` backend by calculating the workspace size and subtracting it from the available memory. This ensures memory is correctly provisioned in all scenarios for the `aiter` backend.

```python
        if (
            self.server_args.attention_backend == "aiter"
            and self.mambaish_config is None
        ):
            from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import AttentionArch
            if self.model_config.attention_arch == AttentionArch.MLA:
                # For MLA, workspace is allocated dynamically, not during init
                max_total_num_tokens = rest_memory_bytes // cell_size
            elif self.server_args.max_running_requests is None:
                # `max_total_num_tokens` is used in `ModelRunnerKVCacheMixin.init_memory_pool` to define
                # `max_num_reqs`, which is in turn used in AITER attention backend to define GPU HBM buffers for the attention.
                # The default strategy below to resolve `max_total_num_tokens` does NOT take into account the memory required for the attention backend, potentially resulting in OOM errors in AITER buffers allocation.
                max_total_num_tokens = self._solve_max_tokens_with_aiter_workspace(
                    rest_memory_bytes, cell_size, num_layers
                )
            else:
                # When max_running_requests is set, max_num_reqs is fixed.
                # We need to account for the AITER workspace memory.
                from sglang.srt.layers.attention.aiter_backend import AiterAttnBackend
                num_head = self.model_config.num_attention_heads // get_attention_tp_size()
                head_dim = self.model_config.head_dim
                max_context_len = self.model_config.context_len
                max_num_partitions = AiterAttnBackend.get_max_num_partitions(max_context_len)
                W = num_head * max_num_partitions * (head_dim * 4 + 8)
                max_num_reqs = self.server_args.max_running_requests
                aiter_workspace = max_num_reqs * W
                max_total_num_tokens = (rest_memory_bytes - aiter_workspace) // cell_size
        else:
            # No workspace overhead for other backends
            max_total_num_tokens = rest_memory_bytes // cell_size
```
